keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria starts the row in 793; the capital moved to Heian-kyō in 794 ('running from 794 to 1185'). 230,061 km2 (identical to the Nara shape); no page opened gives an area. Tsushima (129.2-129.5 E) lies outside every Heian bbox and is added on the Toi page's 'Tsushima and Iki provinces' (1019), the provinces being older than the period. Review fix (jk-01-a-fixed): northern land added. Gazetteer: 29 of Miyagi's 32 cells lie outside the 793 and 800 shapes (26 inside the 814 shape) and 0 of the 21 cells of a 50 km circle at Akita lie inside any Heian shape before 1062; the Nara dossier holds both (Taga 724, Momonofu 758 on the Emishi page; 'In 709, the fort of Ideha was created close to present day Akita', Emishi page) and records no loss: the Akita Castle page has the fort 'moved north' in 733, the court 'decided to abolish the Akita Castle in 770 but withdrew the decision ten years later', expeditions 'in 776, 778, 794, 801 and 811', and puts its abandonment c. 1050 (the Former Nine Years' War), so Akita stays until the 1062 keyframe, which takes it inside the Northern Fujiwara shape.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: between the Former Nine Years' War and the Northern Fujiwara the court's governors held northern Mutsu directly (confidence 2: the pages give the victory, not an administrative map; the grant of the six districts to the Kiyohara is not on them).

correction.text: the realm as drawn plus Tsushima; holds from 1087, when the Northern Fujiwara 'became independent and established themselves in Hiraizumi'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria starts the Northern Fujiwara row in 1094; the page gives 1087. The +130 km2 and the bbox change against the 814 shape are Cliopatria's boundary tidy at the Northern Fujiwara seam, not an event; their land is drawn as a vassal tint (ledger 1087).

correction.text: unchanged shape plus Tsushima; holds 1177 to the end of the state in December 1185 (the Genpei War ended in April), when 'Taira is defeated (Genpei War)' and 'The Kamakura period began in 1185'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria runs the row to 1187 and starts the Kamakura shogunate in 1188; the page ends the period in 1185. The 1177 break is unexplained (identical area).

region.text: the realm ruled from Heian-kyō, 'the eastern end of Honshū' still contested; with the Miyagi forts and the Akita foothold the Nara court held

ledger.note: 794: Emperor Kammu moves the capital to Heian-kyō. 'beginning when the 50th emperor, Emperor Kammu, moved the capital of Japan to Heian-kyō'; 'running from 794 to 1185'. The realm includes the northern land of the Nara dossier (Taga Fort 724, Momonofu 758, Ideha 709: Emishi page) that the 793 shape lacks; the Miyagi part is also the contest zone of ledger/1.

region.text: the Kitakami valley and the Sendai plain, the Isawa and Shiwa Emishi's war zone since 774

ledger.note: 794-811: the Thirty-Eight Years' War continues under the Heian court. 'After making temporary gains in 794' and 'in 797, Kammu appointed a new commander, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro, under the title Seii Taishōgun' (Heian page); in 794 'many key Shiwa Emishi, including Isawa no kimi Anushiko, became allies of the Japanese' (Thirty-Eight Years' War page).

region.text: the Isawa Emishi's land in the Kitakami valley; 'Aterui's surrender in 802'

ledger.note: 802: Aterui surrenders; Isawa submits. 'a desultory campaign that eventually led to Aterui's surrender in 802' and 'many Emishi groups submitted themselves to the imperial government'; the Heian page: 'By 801, the shōgun had defeated the Emishi and had extended the imperial domains to the eastern end of Honshū.' The Isawa and Shiwa castles (802, 803) are not on the pages opened.

region.text: the Kitakami valley and the Sendai plain, the Isawa and Shiwa Emishi's war zone since 774

ledger.note: 811: the Thirty-Eight Years' War ends. 'it was not until 811 that the so-called Thirty-Eight Years' War was over'; 'North of the Kitakami River, the Emishi were still independent.'

region.text: 'semi-autonomous feudal domains in the north' of Honshū, the land later held by the Abe, Kiyohara and Northern Fujiwara

ledger.note: c. 850: the northern Emishi domains as semi-autonomous dependencies. 'By the mid-9th century, most of the land held by the Emishi in Honshū had been conquered' and 'Emishi families created semi-autonomous feudal domains in the north'; the year is rounded from 'mid-9th century'; a vassal tint (rule 4) because the domains answered to the court's Mutsu posts ('Both the Abe and Kiyowara families were almost certainly of Japanese descent').

region.text: 'Tsushima and Iki provinces' and Hakata Bay, 'the Ido, Shima, and Sawara counties of Chikuzen Province'

ledger.note: 1019: the Toi invasion. The Jurchen pirates 'assaulted Tsushima and Iki provinces, beginning on 27 March 1019', wiped out 'the Iki Island garrison, consisting of 147 soldiers', 'on April 9, attacked Hakata' and 'using Noko Island in Hakata Bay as a base, they sacked villages and kidnapped over 1000 Japanese'.

region.text: 'Tsushima and Iki provinces' and Hakata Bay, 'the Ido, Shima, and Sawara counties of Chikuzen Province'

ledger.note: 1019: the Toi driven off. The Dazaifu 'raised an army and successfully drove them away'; they 'raided Matsuura county in Hizen Province from April 13 to May 20' and 'after attacking Tsushima again, they retreated towards the Korean Peninsula'; Goryeo's navy 'rescued around 300 captives'. No land changed hands.

1051: the Abe, 'the general overseeing the Emishi', break with the court. 'In 1050, the general overseeing the Emishi was Abe no Yoritoki, who levied taxes and confiscated property on his own'; the war 'from 1051 to 1062' follows.

region.text: 'Mutsu province, Tohoku region', the Abe clan's lands

ledger.note: 1051-1062: the Former Nine Years' War. Minamoto no Yoriyoshi 'was appointed both Governor and commander-in-chief over controlling the natives'; Sadato 'defeated them at Kawasaki and pursued them through a blizzard' (1057).

region.text: the Abe lands, 'Mutsu province, Tohoku region'

ledger.note: 1062: Kuriyagawa falls. 'In 1062, Minamoto no Yoriyoshi, along with his son, led an assault on an Abe fortress at Siege of Kuriyagawa'; 'After two days of fighting, Sadato surrendered'; result 'Imperial victory'.

region.text: the Abe lands of northern Mutsu

ledger.note: 1062: the Abe lands pass to the court's governors. The page records the victory and reinforcements 'offered by the Governor, a member of the Kiyohara clan, of the nearby Dewa Province', not the grant of the six districts to the Kiyohara; drawn as direct land 1062-1086.

region.text: 'the Mutsu and Dewa Province' north of the Sendai plain, as Cliopatria draws the Northern Fujiwara

ledger.note: 1087: Fujiwara no Kiyohira's realm at Hiraizumi. Kiyohira 'became independent and established themselves in Hiraizumi ... in 1087, when he won the victory in the Gosannen War'. No vassal tint is drawn over the Northern Fujiwara after 1087 (review fix jk-01-a-fixed): the Northern Fujiwara page says they 'were able to keep their independence vis-à-vis Kyoto', and the Fujiwara no Hidehira page says he 'was the official imperial governor for Mutsu Province as of 1181' yet 'controlled his territory independently of the central government'; it has no Chinjufu-shōgun title, tribute or submission, so the earlier 1087-1185 vassal pair (confidence 1) is removed.

region.text: the eastern provinces: 'the provinces of Kai and Kōzuke, where the Takeda and other friendly families helped repel the Taira army', and the Kantō around Kamakura

ledger.note: 1180: the Genpei War reaches the east; the Minamoto hold Kai, Kōzuke and the Kantō. Mochihito 'sent out a call to arms to the Minamoto clan and Buddhist monasteries in May'; Yoritomo 'was defeated by the Taira in the battle of Ishibashiyama' then 'successfully made it to the provinces of Kai and Kōzuke'; infobox 'June 20, 1180 – April 25, 1185'. The page gives no month for the eastern campaign (the infobox date is the war's), so no month is set. The east is drawn as a contest zone against 'Minamoto clan' until the war ends in April 1185 ('Minamoto clan victory'), although 'For nearly two years, the war ceased' (1181-1183), because the Kantō stayed in Minamoto hands; the Kamakura dossier starts only in December 1185, so a rebel dossier 'Minamoto clan' (1180-1185) is requested to carry the mirror. This pair covers the eastern zone only; the western theatre has its own pair (1183).
1180: the capital moves to Fukuhara-kyō (Kobe). 'The capital is moved to Fukuhara-kyō (Kobe)' (June 1180); Kiyomori 'moved the seat of power to Fukuhara-kyō in June 1180' (Genpei page).
1180: the capital returns to Heian-kyō. 'The capital is moved back to Heian-kyō (Kyōto)' (November 1180).

region.text: the Inland Sea, 'their ancestral home territory', where the Taira consolidated after leaving Kyoto: Yashima, Dazaifu, Ichi-no-Tani and Dan-no-ura

ledger.note: 1183: the Taira leave Kyoto and hold the west. The war 'resume[d] in the spring of 1183'; Munemori 'led his army, along with the young Emperor Antoku and the Imperial regalia, to the west'; 'The Taira set up a temporary Court at Dazaifu in Kyūshū' and, 'forced out soon afterwards by local revolts instigated by Go-Shirakawa', 'moved their Court to Yashima'. The page gives no month, so none is set. The western theatre (Chūgoku, Shikoku, Kyūshū) is a second contest pair with its own counterpart; a rival-court dossier 'Taira clan (western court)' (1183-1185) is requested.

region.text: the eastern provinces: 'the provinces of Kai and Kōzuke, where the Takeda and other friendly families helped repel the Taira army', and the Kantō around Kamakura

ledger.note: 1185: the Genpei War ends with 'Minamoto clan victory' (infobox end date April 25, 1185); the Kantō and the rest of the realm pass to Yoritomo's military government, which the Genpei page dates to December 1185 ('Go-Shirakawa granted to Yoritomo ... power to ... appoint stewards and constables in all provinces'). Closes the eastern pair of ledger 'contest_start Minamoto clan' (1180).

region.text: the Inland Sea, 'their ancestral home territory', where the Taira consolidated after leaving Kyoto: Yashima, Dazaifu, Ichi-no-Tani and Dan-no-ura

ledger.note: 1185: Dan-no-ura ends the Genpei War. 'Minamoto clan victory'; 'The Genpei War came to an end one month later, following the battle of Dan-no-ura' (infobox end date April 25, 1185); Emperor Antoku died in the battle. In 1183 Munemori had led the Taira 'along with the young Emperor Antoku and the Imperial regalia, to the west', to Yashima and 'a temporary Court at Dazaifu in Kyūshū'. Closes the western pair opened in 1183.

region.text: the whole realm, governed from 1185 by Yoritomo's military government while the court remained in Heian-kyō

ledger.note: 1185: the Taira defeated; the Kamakura period begins. 'Taira is defeated (Genpei War)'; 'The Kamakura period began in 1185 when the family of Minamoto no Yoritomo seized power'; in December 1185 Go-Shirakawa granted Yoritomo the power to 'appoint stewards and constables in all provinces' (Genpei page). Month: December 1185, the Genpei page's date for the grant of 'stewards and constables in all provinces', so that this state and the Kamakura dossier (found 1185-12) abut; the war itself ended in April 1185 (contest events). The year is the Heian page's, the month a reading of the Genpei page.

wars.name: Thirty-Eight Years' War

zones.text: the Kitakami valley and the Sendai plain, the Isawa and Shiwa Emishi's war zone since 774

wars.outcome: The court took the Isawa Emishi's land with 'Aterui's surrender in 802'; 'it was not until 811 that the so-called Thirty-Eight Years' War was over'; 'North of the Kitakami River, the Emishi were still independent.'
wars.note: Infobox '774–812'. Heian part: 794 temporary gains, 797 Tamuramaro as Seii Taishōgun, 802 Isawa; the Shiwa castle (803) and Fun'ya no Watamaro (811) are not on the page. The war ran 774-811; years clipped to this dossier's life (reviewer jk-01-a), the Nara dossier carries 774-794.

wars.name: Toi invasion

zones.text: 'Tsushima and Iki provinces' and Hakata Bay, 'the Ido, Shima, and Sawara counties of Chikuzen Province'

wars.outcome: Raids of 27 March to 20 May 1019 on Tsushima, Iki, Chikuzen and Hizen; 'Many Japanese girls kidnapped and enslaved'; the Dazaifu drove the pirates off; no land changed hands.
wars.note: '1,280 were taken prisoner, 374 were killed'; Goryeo intercepted the fleet off Wonsan and returned some 270 captives.

wars.name: Former Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: 'Imperial victory' and 'the surrender of Abe no Sadato' after the siege of Kuriyagawa (1062).
wars.note: Kawasaki (1057) was an Abe victory; the Kiyohara governor of Dewa reinforced the court's army. No territorial changes listed on the page; the Abe lands are drawn as direct land from 1062.

wars.name: Gosannen War
wars.outcome: 'Military stalemate' between the Kiyohara factions and Minamoto no Yoshiie, Governor of Mutsu from 1083; 'In the end, Iehira and Narihira were killed'; Fujiwara no Kiyohira, who 'helped' Yoshiie, emerged as lord of the north (Northern Fujiwara page: 1087).
wars.note: Dates '1083–1089 (disputed)'; the siege of Kanezawa '1086–1089'. Fought within the court's own province; no contest events.

wars.name: Hōgen rebellion
wars.outcome: '1156: Taira no Kiyomori defeats the Minamoto clan and seizes power.'

wars.name: Heiji rebellion
wars.outcome: 'In 1159, the Taira and Minamoto clashed (Heiji Rebellion)'; the Taira won.

wars.name: Genpei War

zones.text: the eastern provinces: 'the provinces of Kai and Kōzuke, where the Takeda and other friendly families helped repel the Taira army', and the Kantō around Kamakura
the Inland Sea, 'their ancestral home territory', where the Taira consolidated after leaving Kyoto: Yashima, Dazaifu, Ichi-no-Tani and Dan-no-ura

wars.outcome: 'Minamoto clan victory' (June 20, 1180 – April 25, 1185): the Taira court destroyed at Dan-no-ura; Yoritomo's military government at Kamakura succeeds the Heian state (1185).
wars.note: The Taira held the capital and 'their ancestral home territory' around the Inland Sea; the Minamoto held Kai, Kōzuke and the Kantō; Yoshinaka took Kyoto in 1183 and the Taira fled west with Antoku. Zones and ledger pairs (review fix jk-01-a-fixed): east (Kantō, Kai, Kōzuke) 1180-1185 against 'Minamoto clan'; west (Chūgoku, Shikoku, Kyūshū) 1183-1185 against 'Taira clan (western court)'. The page: 'For nearly two years, the war ceased, only to resume in the spring of 1183'; it gives no date for the Juei edict or for Yoritomo's base at Kamakura.

certainty.note: The northern frontier is a war zone on the Kitakami; provincial limits elsewhere are administrative.
The northern limit against the Emishi domains, the Abe and the Northern Fujiwara is approximate; island limits (Tsushima, Iki, Sado, the Ryukyus) are not drawn on the pages.

notes: Cliopatria 793-1187 against the page's 794-1185; the Kamakura shogunate starts in 1185 (one-year overlap convention). Tsushima is added to every keyframe on the Toi page's 'Tsushima and Iki provinces'; 'Tsushima' and 'Iki' are not gazetteer names yet. The northern story is a reading of thin pages: Isawa added from 802 (Shiwa, 803, not on the pages); the Emishi domains as a vassal tint from c. 850 (Emishi page, confidence 1); the Abe lands direct 1062-1086 (new keyframe, confidence 2); no vassal tint over the Northern Fujiwara after 1087 (removed in the review fix: the Northern Fujiwara and Hidehira pages call them independent). Counterpart 'emishi' has no row; see the Asuka notes. The Minamoto east 1180-1185 is a contest pair with the counterpart 'Minamoto clan' and the Taira's western court of 1183-1185 (Yashima, Dazaifu) a second pair with 'Taira clan (western court)'; both are stand-ins until rebel dossiers exist (listed in the report as counterparts needing dossiers). The dissolve is dated December 1185 (the Genpei page's grant) to abut the Kamakura start. Not on the pages opened: the Gangyō rebellion (878), Taira no Masakado (939-940; his Kantō regime lasted under a year, so no rebel dossier), Fujiwara no Sumitomo (undated on the page), the Isawa and Shiwa castles, the Hiraizumi move, Hokkaido and the Ryukyus. Review fix (jk-01-a-fixed): Miyagi and Akita added to the 793, 800 (and Akita to the 814) keyframes and the found region; Genpei split into two pairs; the Northern Fujiwara vassal pair deleted. Not acted on: the Kiyohara as a vassal tint for 1062-1086 (page not opened), the c. 850 vassal tint (confidence 1), the Isawa and Shiwa castle dates.
